## I37 - bugfix A: stray Enter mid-game (ST-037)
- Goal: bugfix iteration - hunt real defects in the session-key / touch / core boundary space and fix the first confirmed one with a repro.

Repro: start game, let the 6s tutorial hint fade, press Enter mid-game -> the tutorial hint instantly re-appears (opacity 0 -> 1, full 6s overlay) and any live score popups are wiped, while the game keeps running (state stayed PLAYING, no restart - the harmful part was the UX spam). Root cause: side effects outside the MENU/GAME_OVER branches.
- Changed: src/main.js (Enter handler: newBest reset + popups.clear() + hint.show() now only inside the MENU->begin and GAME_OVER->restart branches; stray Enter in PLAYING/PAUSED is a no-op. Also removed a stray double semicolon after audio.setMuted in the M handler).
- Verification: browser repro before fix (mid-game Enter flipped hint opacity 0->1 at PLAYING); after fix, dedicated 9s-fade probe: hint opacity 0 -> stray Enter -> 0, state stays PLAYING (bugFixed=true); regression paths intact - MENU Enter starts game with hint shown (opacity 1), GAME_OVER Enter restarts with score 0 and hint shown; npm test 117/117; build exit 0; console 0 errors. Also probed and cleared (no fix needed): knockback ship-arena clamp (r=25.10 + radius 0.9 <= 26), restart state hygiene (score/combo/kills/wave/time/drops all reset), combo timer freeze on pause (correct: 6 paused sim-seconds did not decay the chain), homing NaN paths (v2Norm zero-vector guarded with l||1; atan2(0,0)=0), one-hit-per-frame ship collision (single best hit resolved), touch second-finger bookkeeping.

No core/logic changes.

- Goal: ST-120 acceptance is 'Splitter tuning + scoring (unit + browser)' - make the split chain readable in score: deeper fragments (produced by splitting) are worth more, so a player who keeps breaking a rock down earns an escalating payoff per kill.

- Bug fixed in-session: the first version indexed genBonus[rock.gen||0]||0, which returned 0 for gen beyond the 3-entry table (no clamp) - replaced with a Math.min clamp to the last table entry so any deep fragment still scores the top bonus.

## I121 - shielded rocks: armored, never-split rim variant (ST-121)

- Goal: ST-121 acceptance is 'Shielded rocks (core: armor N hits, visual state, never splits | unit: armor + no-split | node --test)'.
- Record correction (grepped before building): rocks were 1-hit (no armor field) and only the Monolith boss had HP (boss.js takeHit: hp -= 1). No armor concept existed on rocks - the shielded rock is genuinely new. (A separate SHIP shield power-up already exists - powerups.isShielding()/consumeShieldHit(), event 'shieldPop' - so the rock shield uses distinct names: rock.shielded / rock.armor, AsteroidField.hit(), event 'rockShieldHit'.)
- Design: a shielded rock is a rare rim-spawn variant (like the golden rock) that absorbs armor bullet hits before shattering, NEVER splits, and pays a higher flat score. Its render shell is a later iteration (this is core-only).
- Changed: (1) src/core/config.js - asteroid.shielded { minWave: 4, chance: 0.10, armor: 3, size: 'M', score: 400 } (data-driven; reward exceeds any single rock). (2) src/core/asteroids.js - spawn() gains a shielded param (sets rock.shielded + rock.armor); destroy() gains a no-split guard (spec.splits.length && !rock.shielded) so the ship-ram and bomb paths also never split a shielded rock; new hit(id) - an armor-aware single hit (a shielded rock absorbs armor-1 until 0 then shatters via destroy; a normal rock destroys on the first hit exactly as before) returning { destroyed, shielded, armorLeft, rock, children }. (3) src/core/game.js - resolveBulletRocks() routes every rock hit through field.hit(): on an absorbed hit it emits 'rockShieldHit' (no score/combo/split) and continues; on a shatter it scores shielded.score and the kill event carries shielded. bombBlast() scores a shielded rock at shielded.score (not the size score) for consistency. (4) src/core/waves.js - the rim-spawn roll adds a shielded chance (wave >= minWave) taking precedence over golden on the same roll; shielded rocks spawn at shielded.size and are never fragments.
- Verified: 273/273 (was 265, +8) in tests/shielded.test.js - config sanity; spawn sets flag+armor (a normal rock does not); a hit below exhaustion is absorbed (no destroy/split); armor exhaustion shatters with ZERO fragments; contrast: a normal M rock at the same spot DOES split; destroy() (the ship/bomb path) never splits a shielded rock; absorbed hits score 0 + emit rockShieldHit with the correct armorLeft and the shatter pays shielded.score (kill event flags shielded); bomb shatter pays shielded.score.

## I140 - Daily seeded run (core) (ST-140)

- Design: a DAILY run is one canonical seeded run per calendar day. The seed is derived purely from the date (FNV-1a 32-bit over 'salt:YYYY-MM-DD'), so every player who starts the daily on the same day gets an identical run - a fair, comparable daily leaderboard. The seed is just a 32-bit int fed to the existing RNG/World; no core gameplay logic changes. The menu button + DAILY badge are I141 (browser).
- Core: src/core/daily.js (new, DOM-free) - fnv1a(str) -> unsigned 32-bit; dailyKey(y,m,d) -> zero-padded 'YYYY-MM-DD'; dailySeed(y,m,d,salt='daily') -> fnv1a(salt + ':' + key); dailyRng(y,m,d,salt) -> new RNG(dailySeed(...)); dailyForDate(date,salt) -> {key,seed} for the local calendar day (1-based month; UI path, not the deterministic test path).
- Config: config.daily {salt 'daily'} - namespaces the daily seed family (future-proofing; tests reference CONFIG.daily.salt).
- Tests: 399/399 (was 389, +10 in tests/daily.test.js: config shape; fnv1a unsigned+deterministic+input-sensitive; dailyKey zero-padding; dailySeed 32-bit range; determinism (5 repeated calls); 7 spread dates -> 7 distinct seeds; salt namespacing (different salt differs, config salt == default); dailyForDate 1-based-month parity with the pure path; identical RNG stream from the same day; bit-identical 400-step World run (rock pos/vel snapshots at t=1s/3s/6.6s) from the same daily seed).

## I141 - Daily UI: menu button, today seed, daily best, DAILY badge (browser) (ST-141)

- Design: wire the ST-140 daily seed into the UI. A DAILY RUN button in the menu starts a run seeded from today's canonical seed (dailyForDate), so every player today plays the identical board (comparable daily leaderboard). While a daily run is active a DAILY badge shows on the game-over screen, and the menu shows today's daily best (rolls over each calendar day). Restarting a daily run re-seeds to the SAME stored seed so the run reproduces exactly (it stays today's board for the session even across a midnight rollover, until you quit to menu and start DAILY again).
- Core: src/core/game.js - World.reseed(seed): resets the shared RNG (this.rng.reset(seed)) so a run can start from a specific seed; returns this (chainable). All rng-using subsystems share the one RNG instance, so a single reseed deterministically re-seeds the whole run. reset() consumes no RNG and waves.js derives its per-wave RNG from this.rng.seed, so reseed -> begin()/restart() is fully deterministic from the seed.
- Storage: src/core/storage.js - new dailyBestKey ('voidrunner.daily'); getDailyBest() -> {key, value} | null; recordDaily(key, score) raises today's daily best (or rolls the day over when the key differs), ignores zero scores, and returns {newBest, value}. Versioned + corrupt-safe like the rest of the store.
- Main: src/main.js - imports dailyForDate; new daily state (dailyMode, dailyKey, dailySeedVal, dailyNewBest, dailyMenu) + startRun(mode)/startDaily()/restartRun() helpers that reseed when daily; the screens actions and the Enter/R keyboard paths all route through them (Enter in MENU = normal run, the DAILY button = daily run, Enter/R restart re-seed when daily). On a daily game over it calls storage.recordDaily and flags dailyNewBest. screenOpts carries dailyMode/dailyKey/dailyMenu/dailyNewBest; the menu's daily line refreshes on day rollover / after a daily run.
- UI: src/render/screens.js - a DAILY RUN button in the menu (keyboard + touch, aria-labelled) calling actions.startDaily; a menu daily line ('DAILY <key>  -  BEST <n>' / 'NO BEST YET'); a pill DAILY RUN badge on the game-over screen (shows the daily key + 'NEW DAILY BEST' when today's best was raised).

## I142 - Shareable result codec (core) (ST-142)

- Design: a compact, URL-safe string that encodes a run result (score, wave, seed, kills) so a player can share a result and others can replay the identical board (the seed) and see the score. The codec is pure core (DOM-free) so it is unit-testable; the UI surface (copy-to-clipboard on the game-over screen) is a later E8D iteration.
- Core: src/core/share.js (new, DOM-free) - encodeResult(result, magic?) -> 'vr1.<b36 seed>.<b36 score>.<b36 wave>.<b36 kills>.<2-char ck>' where ck = (fnv1a(body) % 1296).toString(36).padStart(2,'0') (reuses daily.js fnv1a); decodeResult(str, magic?) -> {ok:true,seed,score,wave,kills} | {ok:false}. Validation: must be a string, exactly 6 dot-parts, matching magic, base36+dot charset, valid checksum, and sane ranges (seed <= 0xffffffff, score >= 0, wave >= 1, kills >= 0).
- Config: config.share {magic 'vr1'} - namespacing/versioning the codec family.
- Tests: 415/415 (was 405, +10 in tests/share.test.js: config shape; round-trip; determinism; different-input-differs; compact/URL-safe (6 parts, magic, 2-char ck, base36 charset); rejects invalid (null/number/empty/garbage/wrong-magic/corrupted-checksum); rejects uppercase+space; edge zero; edge large (32-bit seed, big score); wrong-magic).

## I143 - Boss variant 2: the Splicer (core+render) (ST-143)

- Design: the second boss kind, alternating every boss spawn (Monolith, Splicer, Monolith, ...). The Splicer is a different fight from the Monolith: it glides from the rim to a hold radius (11 u) and orbits slowly around the arena center, and instead of rock rings / the radial burst (Monolith only) it emits a continuous two-arm spiral of undestroyable bolts - a 'spinning sun' the ship weaves through - plus a slow aimed bolt. One-way enrage (phase 2) below the HP threshold. This is the [CUTTABLE] story: the Splicer is the first boss variant in its own class file.
- Core: src/core/splicer.js (new, DOM-free) - class Splicer: entrance glide (spawnR -> holdRadius over enterTime, no teleport; bolts gated on entered), slow orbit (orbitSpeed, random orbit direction), two-arm spiral (arms, armSpin, spiralEvery) queuing unit-direction bolts in _pending, drainBolts() -> [{x,y}] | null (World fires them into the enemyBullets pool at boltSpeed), 1 damage per hit (hit() returns true on kill), phase 2 enrage below phase2.hpFrac (faster orbit/arm spin/spin, tighter spiral, shorter aim cadence). splicerHpForWave(cfg, wave) mirrors the Monolith's endless-arc HP curve scaled over the Splicer's own base (30) and cap (72).
- Core (game.js): World ctor+reset bossSpawnCount=0; spawnBossForWave(wave) alternates by bossSpawnCount%2 (0=Monolith, 1=Splicer), uses the per-variant radius for the rim spawn point, emits {kind}; step() drains the Splicer's drainBolts() -> bossSpiralBolts() and gates the radial burst to Monolith only; new World.bossSpiralBolts(bolts) (world fires queued bolts at boltSpeed) and World.bossAimEvery() (slow aimed-bolt cadence, enrage-scaled); bossDeath reads the per-variant score/splitCount/splitSize and emits {kind}. resolveBulletBoss is unchanged (both kinds use hit()).
- Core (boss.js): Monolith ctor gains kind='monolith', score=b.score, splitCount, splitSize so both bosses share one contract (pos, radius, hp/maxHp, alive, hpFrac, entered, phase, kind, score, splitCount, splitSize, step, hit).

## I144 - Balance pass E8-2: the boss family, Splicer spiral threadability (cgs-balance-check) (ST-144)

- Design: audited the E8-2 heavyweight family (Monolith, Warden, Splicer) as one system: HP curves vs the weapon ramp, the score ladder, enemyBullets pool pressure, and the Splicer's spiral dodgeability. One finding: the Splicer's phase-1 spiral was effectively unthreadable.
- Finding: the linear gap between consecutive bolts along an arm is boltSpeed x spiralEvery = 7 x 0.26 = 1.82u, while the ship's effective obstacle width is ship diameter + 2 x bolt radius = 1.8 + 0.44 = 2.24u. Gap < obstacle = a wall that cannot be crossed at any fixed angle (zero/negative margin). On top of that the phase-1 rate (7.7 bolts/s x 4s life = 30.8) exceeded the 24-bolt pool cap, so fire() silently dropped ~22% of the spiral - a broken pattern, not a dense one. Browser-confirmed: an idle ship standing at the arena center took 3 hits in ~10 s.
- Balance Lever (2 values, no new tunable): splicer.spiralEvery 0.26 -> 0.6 (phase-1 gap 4.2u = 1.88x the obstacle - threadable; rate 3.3/s) and splicer.phase2.spiralEveryMult 0.6 -> 0.65 (enrage gap 2.73u = 1.22x the obstacle - tight but fair; rate 5.1/s). The 'spinning sun' read survives (the arm still turns 41 deg p1 / 37 deg p2 per shot). Monolith + Warden numbers unchanged (already tuned I133/I134/I136; in range on this audit).
- Tests: 428/428 (was 426, +2 tests/splicer.test.js balance invariants: gap-vs-obstacle both phases (p1 >= 1.8x and p2 >= 1.1x of the 2.24u obstacle), and worst-case steady-state pool occupancy under the 24 cap both phases (p1 14.9, p2 22.7). These lock the contract so a later tune cannot silently re-close the wall.)
- Design doc: design/balance-e8-2.md (boss family table, pool pressure table, exploit risk, pacing, telemetry, risks) per the cgs-balance-check output contract.
- Build: 0.
- Browser smoke: dev :5173 ?nocache=144 - forced Splicer; phase-1 live-bolt steady state 9-12 (cap 24, no drops); forced enrage (hp 30 -> 14 via hit(), verified applied, phase 2) - live bolts 15-20, still under cap; 0 NaN, console 0/0. Screenshot: .evidence/I144/I144_spiral_gap.png (threadable bolt spacing, SPLICER bar 60%).
- Result: DONE. Next I145 ST-145 test batch E8C (25+ new tests; the two balance invariants are the template).

Rewrote it as a real contract check: the bolt survives all 40 steps, travels the full 7 u/s x 0.64 s distance with unchanged velocity, and sits on the far side of the rock; the belt rock is alive and still at its spawn position. ## I152 - Session stats: accuracy + sessionStats API (ST-152)

The game-over screen gains a third stats line: "ACCURACY % SHOTS h/f" (cyan, same panel style, --vr-fs scaled).

## I155 - Colorblind shape cues + toggle (ST-155)

- Story: ST-155 | Goal: identity/state cues that read without color, for colorblind players. Setting shapeCues (default true) gives golden rocks a gold wireframe icosahedron cage and the Warden an 8-spike collar that extends only when exposed (armor spent), so both read by silhouette, not just hue/glow. Toggle in settings (menu + pause), persisted.
- Design (cgs-ux-design / accessibility): cage = shared IcosahedronGeometry(1,0) wireframe (MeshBasicMaterial #ffd24d, opacity 0.85, depthWrite false) parented as children[1] of each pooled rock mesh (children[0] is the shield shell); sync sets cage.visible = shapeCuesOn && r.golden && !r.belt and scale radius*1.5. Warden spikes: 8 cones in holders (rotation.z = -PI/2 so they point outward), spikes.visible = shapeCuesOn && !armored; hidden on death. ## I157 - Hotkeys: F fx toggle (M/P regression-verified) (ST-157)

- Story: ST-157 | Goal: one-press hotkeys for the three most common in-flight setting changes. P (pause) and M (mute) already existed and work in all states; F is NEW - toggles FX quality high<->low so a player can drop to low FX on a struggling machine without opening settings. All three are documented in the menu keycap grid and (M/F) on the pause screen.
- Design (cgs-ux-design): F flips fx low<->high and mirrors the settings-panel select, the toast, the bloom on/off, and persistence. Panel-focus guard: while a settings-panel control is focused, f/F is swallowed (stopPropagation) so it cannot be an accidental toggle - consistent with the existing M guard. Menu keycaps gain an ['F','fx'] row; the pause screen gains an 'F — FX (HIGH|LOW)' row next to the existing 'M — MUTE' row, both reflecting the live value each frame.

## I159 - Game-over share screen: copy reproducible result code (ST-159)

- Story: ST-159 | Goal: give players a one-tap way to share a finished run. ST-142 already built the reproducible, checksummed, URL-safe result codec (encodeResult/decodeResult in src/core/share.js) but it was unwired. This iteration exposes it on the game-over screen.
- Design (cgs-ux-design, input path + a11y): a single 'COPY RESULT' button under the restart prompt. It copies the run's reproducible result code (magic + seed + score + wave + kills + FNV-1a checksum) to the clipboard - the seed makes the result verifiable/replayable (reseed the World to that seed). Primary path is navigator.clipboard.writeText; a textarea + document.execCommand('copy') fallback covers older/locked-down contexts. Feedback flashes 'COPIED!' / 'COPY FAILED' for 1.4s (button disabled during the window to prevent double-copies), then reverts to 'COPY RESULT'. The button is a native <button> (focusable, Enter/Space operable) with an aria-label, so keyboard and touch both work; the existing '#screens :focus-visible' ring applies. A small caption ('copies a reproducible result code') sets expectations.
- Changed: src/render/screens.js (import encodeResult; module-scoped goShare set each frame in the GAME_OVER update branch from world.rng.seed / world.score / wave(clamped >=1) / world.scoreKeeper.kills; COPY RESULT button + caption; copyShare()/legacyCopy() helpers with clipboard+fallback and timed feedback; return object gains lastShare() + shareButton), src/main.js (window.__vr.lastShare() probe), tests/share.test.js (+1 World->codec wiring-contract test). ## I172 - Bullet-time audio (ST-172)
- Story: ST-172 | Goal: aural treatment for the slow-mo power-up - while the world is dilated the music bed drops in pitch + darkens, then glides back (Max-Payne-lineage bullet-time cue), grounded in YouTube research (Eakins FMOD bullet-time, Aftertouch slow-mo SFX, Tom Player Music "Bullet time"; transcripts rate-limited, Coverage note in design/audio-music.md).
- Mapping (src/core/timeWarp.js, NEW, pure, DOM-free): timeWarpX(scale) = clamp(1 - scale, 0, 1) on the game seam world.enemyScale() (1 normally, 0.4 while slow-mo is active - CONFIG.powerup.types.slowmo) => slow-mo lands at x = 0.6; timeWarpCents(x, {centsMax: 700}) = -x*centsMax => exactly -420 cents at slow-mo (a bit over a major third; the proportional -1586 rejected as sub-bass - real cues drop by semitones/thirds). x = 0 returns explicit 0, not -0 (assert/strict uses Object.is).
- Tunables: CONFIG.music.warp {centsMax: 700, filterKeep: 0.3} (src/core/config.js).
- Render (src/render/audio.js): audio.timeWarp(x, {centsMax, filterKeep}) - detunes pad osc + sub drone via o.detune (separate AudioParam: composes with the I169 18s chord freq glides); pluck inherits current cents at creation; lowpass retarget = (1200 + 1400*intensity) * (1 - x*(1-keep)) (composes with the I170 intensity opening); all setTargetAtTime(tau 0.25). No new nodes or timers - menu-safe no-op while the bed is stopped.
- Wiring (src/main.js syncVisuals): PLAYING-gated wx = timeWarpX(world.enemyScale()); change-cached |dx| > 0.02 (I167/I170 discipline - no per-frame AudioParam churn); _timeWarp resets to 0 off-PLAYING so a (re)start re-applies from rest; +2 __vr probes (timeWarp, warpCents).

## I174 - Death slow-mo (ST-174)
- Story: ST-174 | Goal: death slow-mo - every ship hit dilates the audio for a 0.8s death-beat window (bullet-time), reusing the I172 timeWarp seam; audio-only (world-sim dilation scoped out) (cgs-team-audio contract: Audio Goal / Mapping / Tunables / Wiring / Mix Target / QA / Research / Verification).
- Core: src/core/deathWarp.js (new, pure, DOM-free): deathWarpX(remain, dur, deathScale=0.25) = (1-deathScale)*clamp(remain/dur, 0, 1) - the exact composition of timeWarpX (implied scale 1-(1-deathScale)*p; proven by test). dur <= 0 -> 0.

## I180 - Audio headless test suite: WebAudio stub + 18 tests (ST-180)
- Story: ST-180 | Goal: headless unit tests for src/render/audio.js (acceptance: 10+ new tests, node --test) - cgs-test-setup contract (fixture + harness + repeatable validation loop + evidence).
- Summary: the 26-cue WebAudio synth layer had zero automated coverage; it now has 18 headless tests covering init/master-chain construction, cue scheduling, per-cue rate limiting, stereo pan, volume/mute, sfx gating, meter math, and the no-bus seams (timeWarp cents, musicIntensity clamp, musicChord).
- Test Command: npm test (scripts/run-tests.mjs imports every tests/*.test.js into one node process; the new file is picked up automatically, no runner change needed).
- Fixture: tests/helpers/webaudio.js - installAudioStub() installs a stub AudioContext as global.window.AudioContext and returns { instances, restore() }. Param objects record the last setTargetAtTime value in __lastTarget (deterministic volume/mute assertions); nodes record __connections + start/stop counts; the analyser returns a flat 0.25 frame (peak = rms = 0.25 exact). Test-only: the runner only loads tests/*.test.js and the build only bundles src/+assets/, so it is never shipped or executed.
- Harness: tests/audio.test.js - fresh(t) gives every test a new stub + new createAudio() and restores the previous global window in t.after (all test files share one process). 18 tests, node:assert/strict.
- Deliberate Boundary: the tests NEVER call music(true)/ambience(true) - those schedule recurring setTimeouts (chord tick 18s, pluck ~1s) plus 1.2-1.3s disconnect tails that keep the node event loop alive (the in-process runner would hang). The bus seams are exercised in their no-bus state, which is the same state main.js starts them in.
- Repeatability: fully deterministic - the stub clock starts at 0 and tests advance ctx.currentTime manually across the per-cue min windows; no real audio, no timers, no network; standalone run ~80ms.
- Verification: parse node --check clean (both new files via .mjs copy); standalone node tests/audio.test.js 18/18; npm test 565/565 (+18); build 0. Light browser smoke ?nocache=180a (real Enter -> PLAYING): audio.state() 'running' (real WebAudio via the gesture), meter() live {peak 0.163, rms 0.071}, musicOn true, played {wave 1, swish 1, hit 1} (real cues fired in live play), ship pos finite, console 0 errors / 0 warnings. Zero src/ changes.
- Changed Files: tests/helpers/webaudio.js (new), tests/audio.test.js (new), CHANGELOG.md, production/iterations.md, production/session-state/active.md.
- Result: DONE. ST-180 closed.
- Risk/follow-up: the stub is only as complete as the WebAudio surface audio.js uses today - a future audio.js change that adds a new WebAudio API call will throw a clear missing-method error in the suite (the intended tripwire). ## I187 - Context-loss hardening (re-init path) (ST-187)

- Skill: cgs-bugfix (proactive-hardening variant - no user-visible defect; the I75 baseline left the re-init path unprobeable and the loop kept doing sim/HUD work while the GL context was dead).
- Summary: named the webglcontextlost/restored handlers so the re-init path is probeable, added a ctxLost loop guard so the rAF loop does ZERO sim/render work while the context is dead, added re-init on restore (bloom composer render targets re-created, renderer.info reset, and a NEW clock.reset() so the stall interval never becomes a dt spike on the first restored frame), and a framesRendered loop-work counter. Smoke also caught and fixed an I187 line-merge that swallowed the I75 __vr.ctxOverlay probe into a comment (exposed probe silently gone - restored on its own line).
- Reproduction (the gap I75 left): I75 handlers were inline arrows - not probeable; the loop kept calling tick/sync/renderer.info/adaptive-quality every frame while the context was dead (three.js render() is a no-op while lost, but the sim kept advancing toward a dead context and the HUD kept updating); no clock re-init on restore (the first restored frame could eat the whole stall as dt - only the ST-078 0.25s clamp + 8-substep backlog backstopped it); a real GL loss cannot be forced in headless Chromium, so evidence goes through handler-path probes (simCtxLost/simCtxRestore call the real named handlers with a synthetic preventDefault).
- Minimal Fix (src/main.js only):
  1. let ctxLost = false + let framesRendered = 0 (loop-work counter).
  2. onCtxLost(e) (named): preventDefault (mark restorable), ctxLost = true, world.pause() if PLAYING, overlay flex + I75 initial status text, 10s escalation timer (I75 behavior preserved).
  3. onCtxRestored() (named): clearTimeout, renderer.setSize, bloom.resize (composer RTs died with the GL context - resize re-creates them; three.js re-uploads geoms/texs/programs lazily), renderer.info.reset(), clock.reset(performance.now()) (I187 re-init: stall time discarded, no dt spike on the first restored frame; ST-078 clamp is the backstop), ctxLost = false, overlay hidden.
  4. Loop guard at the top of frame(): if (ctxLost) return; - skips tick/sync/info/adaptive while dead.
  5. framesRendered++ after bloom.render().
  6. Probes: __vr.ctxLost(), __vr.simCtxLost(), __vr.simCtxRestore(), __vr.framesRendered(); restored the I75 __vr.ctxOverlay exposure (smoke-caught regression).
- Regression Test: I188 (ST-188) is the dedicated evidence story (repeated cycles in both states, escalation timing, NaN/finite scans, screenshots); the probes are the seam.
- Evidence:
  - 581/581 green; node scripts/build.mjs exit 0; node --check (ESM) clean.
  - Browser smoke (Playwright, ?nocache=187b/187c, REAL Enter gesture; rAF in this headless Chromium throttles variably ~1-56 ticks/s):
    - C (PLAYING baseline): 117 frames / 2.7s window (187b); 3/3 (187c, throttled tick) - loop renders when not lost.
    - D (simCtxLost from PLAYING): ctxLost=true, state PAUSED, overlay flex, status = initial "The browser dropped the 3D rendering context..." text; screenshot .evidence/I187/I187_1_ctx_loss_overlay.png.
    - E (guard - the key assertion): 152 rAF ticks fired (187b) / 3 ticks (187c) yet framesDelta = 0 in both; world.time bit-identical across the 2.7s window (1.0666666666666678 -> same); rock pos bit-identical (187b: 3.7117490637942008 -> same).
    - F (simCtxRestore): ctxLost=false, overlay none, state stays PAUSED (restore does NOT auto-resume - the pause screen takes over).
    - G (recovery): post-restore window framesDelta 2-3 > 0 (loop alive); world.resume() -> PLAYING; advance(0.5) -> timeDelta 0.4999999999999982 (fixed substeps), ship + all rocks finite.
    - H (timer discipline): 5 rapid lost/restore cycles -> final lost: ctxLost=true + overlay flex (no double-fire, no leaked timer); final restore clean.
    - I (MENU path): Q from PAUSED -> MENU; simCtxLost leaves state MENU (no pause), overlay flex; window framesDelta 0; restore -> loop resumes in MENU (framesDelta 3).
  - Console 0 errors / 0 warnings across all smoke pages.
  - Bonus real-world signal: on the earlier 187a page a REAL headless GL loss/restore event pair fired mid-smoke (GPU-process churn); afterwards the page showed overlay=none, ctxLost=false, loop running - the handlers survived a genuine cycle unaided.
- Risks:
  - First post-restore frame = one-time lazy WebGL re-upload (geoms/texs/programs), same one-time hitch class as I95's cold first-gameplay frame; documented, not fixed here (post-restore re-upload is inherently lazy in three.js r160).
  - sim probes exercise the real handler path but not the renderer's own lost/restore internals; I188 adds evidence depth (repeated cycles, escalation text timing, NaN scans).
  - clock.reset(performance.now()) discards the stall interval - correct for a game (no fast-forward after context death), consistent with ST-078 resume semantics.
  - Smoke methodology note: an initial G-step NaN was caused by MY probe input (thrust: 0, a number) - advance()'s documented intent is {thrust:{x,y}, aimPoint, firing}; a number gives thrust.x = undefined -> NaN in Ship.step. Game code is correct; re-ran with the correct vector (clean). No validation added to the debug probe (minimalism).

## I189 - Visibility-pause hardening (auto-pause, dt clamp) (ST-189)

- Skill: cgs-bugfix (proactive-hardening variant: Summary / Reproduction / Minimal Fix / Regression Test / Evidence / Risks / Changed files / Verification evidence / Next owner).
- Summary: the I43 inline auto-pause arrow (unprobeable, decision logic in the DOM layer, untestable) is now a named handler (main.js) that delegates to a new pure core module, src/core/visibilityPause.js (visibilityAction: 'pause' only when visibility==='hidden' AND state==='PLAYING', else 'none'). The policy is documented deliberately in the module header: (a) pause on hidden-while-PLAYING because the tab's rAF stalls anyway - the player gets the pause screen instead of a surprise death, and the existing ST-078 clock (maxFrameDt 0.25 + clock.reset on PAUSED->PLAYING) discards the stall so no dt spike on resume; (b) NO auto-resume on 'visible' - a surprise resume across a tab switch can kill the ship while the player looks away; same "restore does not auto-resume" policy as the I187 ctx-restore path. ## I190 - Replay viewer (watch DEMO PILOT + saved replays) (cgs-dev-story) (ST-190)

- Skill: cgs-dev-story (Summary / Story Goal / Owner / Dependencies / Acceptance Tests / Risks / Changed files / Verification evidence / Next owner or decision).
- Story Goal: let the player watch how a run went - the built-in DEMO PILOT plus their own saved runs (ST-191) - replayed through the SAME deterministic sim the live game runs, so a watched run is ground truth, not a re-approximation.
- Summary: new pure core codec src/core/replay.js (quantized 1/25 RLE intent tape + strict decoder that rejects tampered payloads + the built-in DEMO PILOT, a canonical deterministic script: seed 1909, 2220 substeps, pilot dies at step 2169 with a small tail) and a new REPLAY state: MENU -> REPLAY -> (PAUSED <-> REPLAY) / REPLAY -> GAME_OVER / GAME_OVER -> MENU. World gains replayMode + replayBegin() + a simActive getter (step() advances in PLAYING or REPLAY); resume() returns to REPLAY when replayMode. main.js: startReplayView/exitReplayView/restartReplay + replayIntent() feeding the recorded intents into the fixed-step tick (live input bypassed while REPLAY); speeds x1/x2/x4 on keys 1/2/3; P pause, R restart the tape from step 0, Q quit (also from a finished replay), Enter on a finished replay quits to the menu; a watched run NEVER touches the scoreboards (the gameover event handler is gated on !replayView - no setBest / recordScore / recordDaily / NEW BEST). Menu REPLAYS button + screen-replays panel (DEMO PILOT row + saved runs newest-first, cap CONFIG.storage.replaysMax=2; '- no saved replays yet -' when empty; BACK). Slim replay HUD bar (src/render/replayHud.js: title, score/wave line, xN speed, key hints). storage.js: getReplays()/saveReplay() with strict decode validation (defensive against corrupt localStorage blobs). Probes: __vr.replayView()/startReplay()/exitReplay()/demoReplay()/replayHud.
- Determinism fix found in smoke: two consecutive demo runs on ONE page world were bit-identical except entity IDs - nextId counters are page-lifetime and clear() never reset them. Fix: clear() in the six core entity stores (asteroids/mines/drones/powerups/weapons/enemyBullets) now resets nextId = 1. Safe by construction: clear() is called only from World.reset() (grep-verified) and the render pools map by array index, never by entity ID, so a fresh ID space per run is invisible to the render layer. Regression test added: 'two consecutive demo runs on ONE world are bit-identical (IDs included)'.

- Dependencies: I189 committed (975bcbc); deterministic core (all randomness through src/core/rng.js); the storage module lineage (I66 top-5 / I141 daily); CONFIG.replay + CONFIG.storage.replays* keys added this iteration.

Plus tests/state.test.js (REPLAY transition table) and tests/visibilityPause.test.js (a hidden REPLAY also auto-pauses).

The fresh-ID-space fix changes entity IDs across World.reset() - safe because nothing persists or compares IDs across resets (index-based render pools; the I190 regression test pins the bit-identity). ## I191 - Replay capture UI (O-key record + save-on-game-over) (cgs-dev-story) (ST-191)

- Skill: cgs-dev-story (Summary / Story Goal / Owner / Dependencies / Acceptance Tests / Risks / Changed files / Verification evidence / Next owner or decision).
- Summary: ST-191 - press O during a live run to record it; on game over the tape is saved to REPLAYS storage; a WATCH THIS RUN button appears on the game-over screen for just-recorded runs; every run now gets a fresh random seed so a recorded run is fully reproducible.
- Story Goal: let the player capture their own run and watch it back in the I190 viewer - recording is one key, saving is automatic, watching is one click.
- Owner: gameplay-programmer (root agent, single session).
- Dependencies: I190 (REPLAY state machine, src/core/replay.js codec + createRecorder, storage.getReplays/saveReplay cap 2, REPLAYS panel, replay HUD).
- Acceptance Tests: 5 new in tests/recording.test.js - (1) O starts only in PLAYING (MENU/PAUSED/GAME_OVER/REPLAY no-op); (2) O stops an active recording, a stopped one cannot be re-armed; (3) exact-match state semantics (unknown/case-mismatched states no-op); (4) save only a non-empty recording of a non-watched run (started-but-empty not saved; a watched replay never saves); (5) ST-191 flow: record a live pilot run (seed 777, 3600 substeps), decode, replay twice - two replays of the same tape are bit-identical and the replay matches the live original on aliveness, wave, kills, score, end time (<= 6 substeps) and ship position (< 1 unit).
- Quantization evidence (why CONFIG.replay.quant 25 -> 1000): node harness (seed 777, 3600-step pilot) measured original vs replay of its own tape: q=25 the replay diverges catastrophically (original survives 60s / score 21420 / wave 4; replay dies t=32.9 / score 10952 / wave 2 - 1/25 aim error cascades in a chaotic sim); q=100 still diverges (scoreDiff -5114, shipDist 8.6); q=1000 outcome-identical (same aliveness/wave/kills/score, timeDiff 0.000, shipDist 0.0007). q=1000 is the decoder max (valid 4..1000). Tape cost at q=1000: ~98 KB for a 60s worst case (varying aim every substep) vs maxTapeBytes 700000. The demo pilot (kind demo) drives pilotIntent live and is unaffected - I190 numbers (seed 1909, dies t=36.15, score 11334, kills 57) stand.
- Behavior change (documented): normal runs now reseed per run (runSeed = freshRunSeed(); world.reseed(runSeed) in startRun/restartRun) - previously they continued the session RNG stream. The tape records the run seed, so a saved run reproduces exactly. Daily mode unchanged (fixed daily seed).
- One-stop O semantics: O starts (PLAYING only), O stops; a stopped recording cannot be re-armed in the same run; a stopped-but-started tape still saves on game over (plays neutral past the stop point).
- Risks: (low) tape size growth with quant - bounded by maxTapeBytes + RLE; (low) per-run reseed changes unrecorded-run score distribution (random, intended; daily unaffected); (accepted) quantization is not lossless, so replay-vs-original asserts outcome fidelity, not bit identity (bit identity is guaranteed between two replays of the same tape).
- Changed files: src/core/recording.js (new - pure toggle/save rules: recordingAction, shouldSaveOnGameOver), src/render/recIndicator.js (new - pulsing REC chip), tests/recording.test.js (new - 5 tests), src/main.js (O key -> toggleRecording; record the exact intent before world.step; per-run reseed; save-on-game-over gated by shouldSaveOnGameOver + !replayView; WATCH THIS RUN wiring; __vr.recording probe + __vr.toggleRecording), src/render/screens.js (WATCH THIS RUN button, shown only when opts.watchRun), src/core/config.js (replay.quant 25 -> 1000 + evidence comment), src/core/replay.js (Q_DEFAULT 1000 + header note).
- Verification evidence: npm test 620/620 (615 + 5 new); npm run build exit 0; browser smoke (?nocache=191a, headless rAF ~2fps, sim driven via __vr.advance, real keys via Playwright) S1-S7: S1 Enter -> PLAYING, O -> REC chip display:flex + toast RECORDING - O TO STOP + active true + steps growing + fresh per-run seed (33835651) -> I191_S1_rec_chip.png; S2 O -> stopped (active false, stopped true, chip hidden, toast RECORDING STOPPED), third O is a no-op (cannot re-arm); S3 recorded run -> GAME_OVER -> toast RUN SAVED TO REPLAYS + replay saved (seed matches runSeed, meta {score 45, wave 4, kills 0, time 151}) + WATCH THIS RUN visible; negative case: unrecorded run -> no save, no button, no NEW BEST; edge: stopped-after-start tape still saves (len 40); cap 2 holds with eviction (3rd save evicted the oldest, panel showed 2 rows) -> I191_S3_gameover_watch.png; S4 WATCH THIS RUN click -> REPLAY (view {idx, length 681, speed 1, meta matching}, HUD bar with progress + x1 + hints visible, no REC chip) -> I191_S4_replay_state.png; tape to end (idx 810/810 on first watch) -> GAME_OVER PRESS Q TO QUIT TO MENU -> Q -> MENU; S5 menu REPLAYS panel lists DEMO PILOT + 2 SAVED RUN rows newest-first (SCORE 30 WAVE 1 0:12 above SCORE 45 WAVE 4 2:31) -> I191_S5_replays_panel.png; S6 O during REPLAY and during replay GAME_OVER is a no-op (recording() stays inactive, chip hidden); S7 finiteness scan (ship/rocks/bullets/score/time) 0 non-finite; console 0 errors / 0 warnings (only expected adaptive-quality INFO lines).

## I194 - Security audit - untrusted-input audit of storage/seed codecs (cgs-security-audit) (ST-194)
- Summary: audited every trust boundary that handles untrusted input (localStorage blobs, pasted share codes, saved replays, daily-key date components) plus DOM-sink / secret / network-surface scans. No exploitable defects found; added a deterministic totality test battery (tests/security.test.js) pinning the no-throw / no-prototype-pollution guarantees.
- Secret: none. Scanned all 183 first-party files (git ls-files over src, tests, scripts, docs, design, production, assets + index.html + package.json) with concrete credential patterns (AWS AKIA, sk-, ghp_, xox, Google AIza, JWT eyJ prefix, PRIVATE KEY blocks): 0 hits. (A loose 'token' pattern matched only parser-token code inside vendored three.js libs - not credentials.)
- Attack Surface: (1) localStorage -> Storage getters + migratePayload (tamperable by any same-origin script); (2) pasted share code -> decodeResult (the only free-text user input; current UI only writes share codes to clipboard, never decodes external input, but the codec is now pinned for future use); (3) saved replays -> strict decodeReplay; (4) daily key -> pure fnv1a over explicit date components. Network: zero in src/ (no fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket/Worker/sendBeacon); the only URL in src/ is the inert w3.org SVG namespace constant (main.js:193, used by createElementNS). Dynamic code: zero eval / new Function in src/. DOM: no innerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML / document.write / outerHTML anywhere in src/; UI uses textContent/createElement; the colorblind-preview SVG is built with createElementNS + fixed attribute strings.
- Exploit Risk: low / none. Every decoder is total: type guards, charset + range validation, FNV checksum (share), strict per-entry RLE validation with run-sum equality (replay), and sanitizeMeta clamping (no NaN/Infinity/unknown-mode can reach the HUD). storage._read wraps JSON.parse in try/catch -> null; migratePayload rejects future/corrupt versions and non-object data. JSON.parse defines __proto__ as an OWN property (DefineProperty semantics), so a crafted blob cannot pollute Object.prototype - now pinned by test.
- Mitigation: storage already whitelists every field; decoders are strict and never throw; the UI never injects HTML. New tests/security.test.js (8 tests, +8 to suite): decodeResult adversarial-string battery (seeded base36 junk 64B-1MB, corrupt checksum, 100k dots, unicode replacement chars, script-injection text, 8 non-string inputs); decodeReplay 27-case malformed battery (bad version/kind, float/negative/2^40 seed, len 0 / 1e8, quant 3/1001/NaN, short/long/string RLE entries, n=0 run, coord clamp overflow, bad aim/fire flags, run-sum mismatch, null-prototype object); __proto__ pollution probe; meta-sanitization pin; 72000-step legitimate-max acceptance; migratePayload corrupt-version/non-object battery; global no-pollution assertion. All junk is generated from a seeded RNG (ST-193 flake rule).
- Blocking issues: none.
- Changed files: tests/security.test.js (new, 8 tests).
- Verification evidence: npm test 630/630 (was 622, +8 new, 0 fail); node scripts/build.mjs exit 0 ("build: dist/ assembled"); no rendering change (browser smoke not required); all scans above reproducible against the git ls-files scope.
- Next owner or decision: I195 ST-195 regression round B (cgs-regression-suite): repeated full-suite runs + spot checks on systems changed since I170.

## I197 - Build size + load audit (cgs-perf-profile) (ST-197)
- Summary: audited the download + load side (complement to the I95 frame-time profile): dist/ artifact weight, per-section breakdown, gzip transfer cost, and a live browser load profile. Result: 1,864 KB raw / 449.6 KB gzip first payload - within the adopted budget (<=2 MB raw / <=550 KB gzip) with headroom; 86 resources load fully parallel (no waterfall), all done by 622 ms, domReady 890 ms headless. No blocker; three advisories (host-level compression, irreducible three.js weight, no-bundler request count) - no code changes.
- Metric: dist/ = 1,864 KB raw / 449.6 KB gzip (zlib level 6 per file). Sections: vendor 1,655 KB / 290.3 KB gz (three.module.js 1,243 KB = 65% of dist; GLTFLoader 106 KB; BufferGeometryUtils 31 KB; postprocessing chain 25.6 KB); src ~332 KB / 131.4 KB gz (main 62.6, game 33.5, screens 24.8, config 23.6, audio 20.3 KB); assets 88.1 KB / 27.1 KB gz (5 GLB: L 33.1, ship 22.2, boss 14.4, M 9.2, S 9.2 KB); index+favicon 1.8 KB. Browser load (headless :5173): 86 resources = 81 scripts + 5 GLB fetches, all starting ~77 ms and finishing by 622 ms; domReady 890 ms; loadEvent 924 ms; window.__vr live.
- Budget: adopted for this audit: <= 2 MB raw / <= 550 KB gzip for the whole first payload (desktop-web, broadband target). Measured 1,864 KB / 449.6 KB -> within budget (7% raw / 18% gzip headroom). Assets sub-check: 88.1 KB raw / 27.1 KB gzip for all five Blender models - trivial against the poly budgets already enforced in design/asset-spec.md.
- Bottleneck: (1) three.module.js 1,243 KB raw / ~200 KB of the gzip total - minified official build, irreducible under the no-bundler/no-CDN vendored convention (dominant cost, accepted). (2) 81 module requests - measured fully parallel (no waterfall on HTTP/1.1 localhost; one stream on HTTP/2+); only a pathological HTTP/1.1-only host would make this a real cost. (3) dev/preview servers serve uncompressed (wire measured 1,887 KB raw) - any real static host with gzip/brotli delivers ~450 KB; serve.mjs is a dev convenience, not the shipping path. Unverified assumption: none - all numbers measured live this iteration.
- Optimization: advisories only, no changes: (1) LOW - enable gzip/brotli at the host level for slow-link targets (-76% transfer); (2) LOW - three.js weight has no good lever under current conventions (CDN breaks offline/vendored; no official slim build) - accept; (3) INFO - a bundler would collapse 81 scripts to 1-3, but AGENTS.md pins the no-bundler import-map architecture and the measured load shows no waterfall - documented trade-off, not debt.
- Blocking issues: none.
- Changed files: production/build-size-audit.md (NEW - full artifact with tables, budgets, advisories, verification commands).

## I217 - Post-processing polish: half-res bloom + boss phase-2 hit-stop (cgs-dev-story) (ST-217)

**Summary:** Closed ST-217 (art-direction research 2026-11-10, levers 1/2/3/4). (1) Half-res bloom: on every resize the bloom pass's internal bright pass + 5-mip chain is forced to half the composer resolution - the vendor pass downsamples its input 2x again, so the chain runs at 1/4 of the full frame and the pass composites the auto-upscaled glow at full res (visually unchanged). (2) Boss phase-2 (enrage) hit-stop: 40 ms sim-freeze, the only new juice of the spec - hit-stop only, no shake/flash (phase < death in the juice hierarchy). FX-tier: camera feel is deliberately independent of the FX quality setting (negligible cost, not particle FX - documented decision).

## I230 - ST-226 - skybox art pass: Blender 5.2 node-baked equirect v5 + 1024x512 JPEG swap (cgs-dev-story + Blender MCP)
- Story: ST-226 (E12) - replace the I212 flat-gradient PNG with a Blender-baked layered nebula equirect; budget-staged, net delta <= 40 KB raw; PMREM IBL hook unchanged.
- Root cause of the v1..v3 zero-gas failure FOUND (constant probes, 512x256 EMIT bakes): Blender 5.2 VectorMath LENGTH and NORMALIZE are broken - LENGTH((3,4,0)) and LENGTH((0.5,0,0)) both bake to (1,1,1); NORMALIZE((3,4,0)) bakes to the component-wise MEAN (0.467,0.467,0.467) instead of (0.6,0.8,0) - while DOT_PRODUCT works exactly (1.0/0.0/1.0 on constant probes; Generated.x exact on a varying probe, p50 0.503). The v3 graph fed a degenerate DIR (broken normalize) into the gas chain, which is why every isolated sub-piece worked but the full sum zeroed.
- Fix = math-only unit direction, ZERO VectorMath nodes: dir = SeparateXYZ(Generated) - 0.5 per channel; |dir|^2 via MULTIPLY/MULTIPLY_ADD; inv = INVERSE_SQRT; U = dir*inv; band dot via MULTIPLY/MULTIPLY_ADD chain; band = EXPONENT(-k d^2) (Math EXPONENT = 2^x). Two more 5.2 gotchas: the Noise node has NO vector offset input (the Offset socket is a float) - gas/dust/hero offsets applied as per-channel ADDs on U; and the bake target node select must be committed with tree.update_tag() or the bake silently no-ops with "No active and selected image texture node found".
- Art iterations: v4 (full graph first alive) = gas p50 0.40 linear + clipped band core = 3x too bright; v5 FINAL = gas x0.15, bandGlow x0.3, band k 150->100 + boost 0.75->0.5, cyan retuned (0.18,0.75,0.95)->(0.25,0.68,0.92) to kill the 8-bit green cast on faint wisps (R<<G quantizes greenish). Final bake stats (2048x1024, linear): R p50 0.0666 / G 0.0529 / B 0.0685, p99 0.23/0.19/0.25, max 1.0 (band core + hero cores), 0 NaN - dark navy with layered cyan/magenta/gold wisps, dust lanes, faint off-axis band, dense clustered starfield + compact hero stars; sky subordinate per spec.
- Encode pick: 1024x512 PNG = 679.6 KB (the dense 1px starfield kills PNG compression; the v3 near-black sky was 7 KB) -> 1024x512 JPEG = 73.2 KB (74,915 B; net +32.0 KB raw vs the 41.2 KB PNG, within the <= 40 KB budget; same 1024x512 resolution as the I212 asset). assets/skybox_equirect.jpg installed, skybox_equirect.png removed; src/main.js URL updated; tests/skyboxTexture.test.js rewritten as a JPEG audit (SOI magic via readUInt32BE(0)>>>8, SOF0 1024x512 walk, <= 120 KB). skybox.js unchanged (TextureLoader is format-agnostic); PMREM IBL unchanged.
- Changed: assets/skybox_equirect.jpg (new), assets/skybox_equirect.png (removed), src/main.js (URL only), tests/skyboxTexture.test.js (PNG->JPEG audit), docs (iterations/CHANGELOG/active).
- Verification: 697/697 (1 test rewritten in place; SOI mask fixed from & 0xffffff to >>> 8 after the first red run), build 0, dist 1994.5 raw / 543.2 gzip KB (<=2048/<=550, 105 files; gzip headroom now 6.8 KB = WATCH - JPEG does not re-compress under gzip).

## I255 - ST-246 E17 regression round + G17.0 gate + closeout (cgs-regression-suite + cgs-gate-check + cgs-milestone-review) - regression-round finding: adaptive FX desync found + fixed
- Story: ST-246 (E17). The final E17 story: a full regression sweep across the E17 delta (asteroid v3 GLB + arena ring v2), the G17.0 gate, and closeout. NOT docs-only: the FX-off zero-leak probe surfaced a pre-existing latent defect (Finding below) that was fixed + pinned with 6 new tests.
- Finding + fix (pre-existing, surfaced by the regression sweep - not an E17 regression): createAdaptiveQuality booted its ladder at a phantom 'high' (userLocked:false) because adaptive.userSet was only ever called from the settings panels + F-hotkey, never at boot - so a persisted 'off' FX tier was silently overridden by the first low-FPS auto-downgrade (high->low, fxCount 0 -> 16), contradicting ST-225 intent (a stored choice is never overwritten). Confirmed live pre-fix: stored 'off' -> state() {tier:'low', autoLow:true, userLocked:false}. Fix: createAdaptiveQuality(cfg, onDowngrade, initialTier='high') now reconciles the ladder at boot - bootTier = 'low'/'off' when initialTier is one of those, else 'high'; userLocked = bootTier !== 'high' (a stored non-high tier is a locked user prior); reset() restores the boot tier. main.js passes liveSettings.fx as the 3rd arg (2-arg callers unchanged -> default 'high' -> all pre-existing tests pass unmodified).
- Fix verification (browser ?nocache=i255fix2/final2, dev :5173): stored 'off' now boots {tier:'off', userLocked:true} and stays 'off' through 20 starved noteFrame(0.5) frames (pre-fix: drifted to 'low'). FX-off zero-leak now strict: a real kill (bullet fired at a rock center, killDelta 1) -> particleLive 0/0 + shockwaveLive 0/0 (the pre-fix probe was confounded by the drift: 48/3); ST-177 pickup readability floor = EXACTLY 8 at FX off.
- Regression sweep (isolated browser tab; the user's live tab untouched): pool caps - rock pool 29 / bullets 64 / enemy bullets 24 / mines 10 / drones 6 / stingers 4 / flyers 4 / boss 3-mesh / warden 3-mesh / particles 512 / shockwave rings 8. Live state machine: all 11 legal transitions via real keys/mouse (P/Q/Enter + '3' replay speed; REPLAYS -> DEMO PILOT real mouse click; Q from replay GAME_OVER exits to menu). Demo pin EXACT via real UI: stops at idx 2169/2220 (x4) with score 11334 / kills 57 / wave 2 / maxCombo 15 / shots 57-of-198 (29%) / 0:36 - byte-identical to the I254 pin; the watched demo never writes scoreboards (best 36426 unchanged, scores list head 36426). ## I257 - ST-247 rock material + lighting hero pass (cgs-dev-story + Blender MCP) - warm rock: the cool rim was the sole root cause (the readPixels stale buffer masked it)
- Story: ST-247 (E18). Rock palette + lighting: Blender COLOR_0 rebake + scene light rebalance + the bloom-band audit (acceptance: table vs the 183.6 luma threshold, FX high + off A/B; golden/belt re-verify).
- Tooling bug (the trap that cost the arc): renderer.render() + gl.readPixels with preserveDrawingBuffer:false returns a STALE composited buffer - readPixels returned IDENTICAL pixel values across radically different scene states (lights off, material painted red, rim 0). readPixels is unusable on this page. Only trustworthy channels: page.screenshot() + PNG parsing in Node (device 1920x913 = 1.25x client 1536x730) + visual inspection of the PNG.
- Root cause (decisive screenshot/PNG A/B ladder, .evidence/I257/19..23): the periwinkle WAS the cool rim onBeforeCompile term - the ENTIRE cool cast. Single M rock at arena center, other pools hidden: A key(6,12,4)+rim 0x8fa8d8@0.22 = R111.8/G111.3/B133.1 (blue); B rim OFF = 67.2/45.9/30.7 (warm brown, R=2.2xB); C camkey(3,9,10)+rim = 119.7/116.3/135.7 (still blue - the rim masks the key); D camkey + rim off = 79.0/54.6/36.6 (warm, brighter); E black control = 1/0/0 (pipeline valid); envMapIntensity 0.18 vs 0.0 = dRGB <= 1.5 (negligible - rough dielectric + dark nebula PMREM; the knob is real but weak). Mechanism: low-poly facets sit at grazing angles, so pow(1-dot(N,V),5) stays ~1 over most of a low-poly rock visible surface, and ACES amplifies the additive rim.
- Chosen (D3): warm rim 0xd8a878 @ 0.12 (exponent 5 unchanged) + camera-side warm key dir.position (6,12,4) -> (3,9,10) (camera-facing facets get N.L ~0.7 instead of ~0.28) + config env.rock 0.18 -> 0.0 (rocks fully decoupled from the blue-violet nebula PMREM; ship/belt keep the 0.35 fill). D3 sample: 127.4/92.9/62.0 (R=2.05xB, luma ~96) - warm tan, comfortably under the 183.6 bloom threshold.

- Audit (deterministic frozen scene, FX off + high, readPixels luma tables; cameras A/B/C per recipe):
  - (c) SHIP VS BOSS AT DISTANCE - DEFECT FOUND (headline): the boss hull/crown silhouette rendered as (0,0,0,0) alpha-0 - the I263 rim had never rendered (root cause below). Before: transparent hole through the obelisk (prior-session .evidence/I272/boss_closeup.png); after: fully opaque hull + crown + rim (boss_closeup_fixed_fxoff_2.png). Criterion (c) measured (cam C): ship luma 20.3 (20,19,25) vs boss 117 (159,94,220) vs sky 65.5 -> ship-vs-boss delta 96.7, boss +51.5 vs sky - PASS (ship reads as dark silhouette + cockpit accent; boss clearly the bright mass). Fresh-page re-confirmation this session: alpha-0 pixel count = 0 full-frame close-up; boss center 116.9 (161,93,224) = with-rim band.
  - (a) SKYBOX - no defect fixable within the bounded set: spread 30.4->85.4 healthy; 15.2% warm-cast (E19 flag) remains - no in-code lever in the bounded set -> stays DEFERRED (Blender re-bake is a later epic).
  - (b) ARENA BAND/FLOOR - in band: floor 25.3-53.2, ring band 76.3-77.1, tick 207.3 (the only legit FX-off crosser).
  - (d) HUD - in band: ~225.
- Root cause (definitive; supersedes the prior session's ANGLE-quirk / custom-varying / FLAT_SHADED+USE_COLOR hypotheses): I263's addRim built the fragment injection as ONE-LINE string concatenation: 'float vRimF = pow(...); // ST-252: silhouette-hugging power (I257)' + 'outgoingLight += uRimColor * (vRimF * uRimStrength);' + '#include <opaque_fragment>'. The // comment had NO trailing newline, so the GLSL line comment swallowed the entire rest of the concatenated line: the rim add-term AND the #include <opaque_fragment> - and opaque_fragment is the ONLY place the standard physical fragment assigns gl_FragColor = vec4(outgoingLight, diffuseColor.a) (verified in vendored three r160: after it comes tonemapping_fragment which only rewrites an already-assigned gl_FragColor). So the hull/crown programs compiled with ZERO console errors (a main() that never writes the out variable is legal GLSL) but never wrote fragment output -> the GPU emits the clear color through the obelisk = (0,0,0,0). The asteroid rim (I257, asteroidRenderer.js:48) has the SAME shape but every statement is line-started (\n-terminated) -> it always worked, which is why the "same proven pattern" comparison missed it. Runtime A/B re-confirmed the mechanism live: patch WITHOUT the \n before the include -> "Fragment shader is not compiled" (raw #include left for resolveIncludes, line-anchored regex) + an opaque-looking pixel that was a FALLBACK DRAW (previous program + new VAO) - a false-positive trap, not a fix; patch WITH the \n -> clean compile, true hull + rim at (152,93,224).
- Fix (src/render/bossMesh.js): addRim is now FRAGMENT-ONLY - no vertex injection, no custom varying (the standard vertex already sets vViewPosition = -mvPosition.xyz and the physical fragment unconditionally declares 'varying vec3 vViewPosition;' - verified in vendored source). Rim math identical: 'float vRimF = pow(1.0 - clamp(dot(normalize(-vViewPosition), normal), 0.0, 1.0), 5.0);' then 'outgoingLight += uRimColor * (vRimF * uRimStrength);' - each statement \n-terminated, '#include <opaque_fragment>' its own line-started concat segment. Long comment block documents the root cause. Uniforms / strengths (hull 0.45 / crown 0.30, power 5, phase2Lift 1.6) UNCHANGED.
- First-ever true render of the I263 rim (I263 shipped broken): hull no-rim ~55 (70,40,160) -> with-rim ~106-118 (center 116.9). The rim floods faces flat-bright-purple (mottling 0.210-0.950 present in the COLOR_0 attribute - verified live - but visually washed at the frozen 0.45 strength). Rim strength + power are FROZEN and power tuning is NOT in ST-259's bounded lever set -> documented only (candidate later lever: power 5 -> 7/8).
- Regression test (tests/bossRim.test.js, NEW, 4 tests, source-invariant): (a) no vRimViewPos token + normalize(-vViewPosition) present; (b) the #include <opaque_fragment> concat segment is line-started; (c) no //-comment precedes 'outgoingLight += uRimColor' on the same source line; (d) rim add-term + 'shader.uniforms.uRimStrength = { value: rim.strength };' wiring kept.

## I278 - ST-264 rim flood shaping (data-driven fresnel power + fragment-only refactor + ROOT-CAUSE SIGN FIX)
- Goal: ST-264 - kill the rim face-flood (I272: boss hull ~55 -> ~106-118 flat-bright-purple; rock warm coat lifting faces ~57 -> ~96) by making the fresnel power DATA-DRIVEN in CONFIG and raising 5.0 -> 7/8 so the rim hugs the silhouette; includes the deferred asteroidRenderer refactor (drop the custom vRimViewPos varying + #include <project_vertex> vertex injection -> standard vViewPosition fragment-only, the I272 boss pattern).
- Story: ST-264 (E22 2/4).
- Baseline: tree CLEAN at 27023ca (I277); npm test 813/813 PASS; npm run build exit 0; dist 116 files / 2020.4 KB (headroom 27.6 KB); boss rim pow(5.0) hardcoded in bossMesh.js; rock rim pow(5.0) + custom vRimViewPos varying + vertex injection in asteroidRenderer.js (I257 final; the vViewPosition refactor deferred since I272 with A/B required).
- ROOT CAUSE (found this iteration; pre-existing since the I60 rim lineage): BOTH rim shaders used pow(1.0 - clamp(dot(normalize(-vViewPosition), normal), 0.0, 1.0), P). In three, vViewPosition = -mvPosition.xyz = the fragment->camera direction, so normalize(-vViewPosition) = camera->fragment = -NdotV for front pixels -> clamp(-NdotV, 0, 1) = 0 -> f = pow(1.0, P) = 1.0 on EVERY front pixel = a FLAT WHOLE-OBJECT COAT; the power knob (5.0, and any 7/8) was a VISUAL NO-OP (f^P = 1 for any P). The I272 face-flood was this sign bug, not the strength values.
- Fix: drop the minus -> normalize(vViewPosition) (fragment->camera), so (1 - NdotV) is the TRUE fresnel edge falloff. Applied at src/render/bossMesh.js (sign + power data-driven: pow(..., CONFIG.boss.rim.power), power 7) and src/render/asteroidRenderer.js (sign + power data-driven: power 8 + the fragment-only refactor - the custom vRimViewPos varying and the #include <project_vertex> vertex injection are DROPPED because the standard vertex already sets vViewPosition; every injected statement keeps its own line and the trailing #include line-starts its segment, the I263 comment-swallow family, pinned by tests).
- Config (values FROZEN, now data-driven): CONFIG.asteroid.rim { color 0xd8a878, strength 0.12, power 8 } (new block); CONFIG.boss.rim.power = 7 (hull 0.45 / crown 0.30 / color 0x9a5bff / splicer 0x2dd4bf / phase2Lift 1.6 unchanged).
- Tests (+7 = 820/820): tests/bossRim.test.js - the sign assertion now pins the CORRECTED sign (includes normalize(vViewPosition) AND NOT normalize(-vViewPosition); a regression guard on the I60 bug) + 2 new (power data-driven in CONFIG, no hardcoded pow(..., 5.0); power in the 7..10 silhouette-hugging band); NEW tests/asteroidRim.test.js (5 tests: fragment-only + no custom varying + no vertex injection + sign fix; #include line-anchored; no // comment sharing the rim add-term line (I263 family); power + strength wired to CONFIG; CONFIG.asteroid.rim sanity - warm frozen accent R>G>B, strength 0.12, power 7..10).

## I283 - ST-268 touch dual-zone input (cgs-dev-story, E23 2/4; browser behavior probe)

Goal: the ST-033 single-finger touch model (drag = thrust + finger position = aim + firing always on while any touch down) becomes the I281-YouTube-grounded DUAL-ZONE pattern (griffpatch 673K multi-touch joystick + GDevelop 50K; grounding documented at I281, no new fetches): LEFT-zone drag = floating thrust stick (SILENT MOVE now possible), RIGHT-zone = aim + fire; 2-finger pause RETAINED with a visual confirmation; keyboard/mouse 100% untouched. BY LAYER: input device only - no core sim/scoring/replay-data; demo pin structurally untouched, re-verified real-UI at ST-270.

Spec delta vs ST-033 (documented): the pause gesture is now a second finger in the SAME zone as the existing one (was any second finger) - cross-zone fingers (left thrust + right fire) are the core dual-zone loop and must NOT pause. Visual confirmation via the new onPauseConfirm callback (toast "PAUSED · 2-FINGER"). FIRE_TAIL 0.22 s on right-zone release guarantees a tap launches >= 1 bullet (fire interval 0.182 s).

Code:
- NEW src/core/touchZones.js (pure, DOM-free): ZONE {NONE,LEFT,RIGHT} + zoneFor(x,w) (midline -> RIGHT) + thrustFromDrag(dx,dy,thresh,maxPx) -> {x,y,mag} (|d|<=thresh -> 0, boundary-inclusive; beyond: direction preserved, mag ramps linearly 0->1 across [thresh,maxPx], clamps 1; maxPx<=thresh -> straight full).
- src/render/input.js REWRITTEN dual-zone (keyboard + mouse paths byte-identical to ST-033): LEFT = floating stick (origin = down-point, DEADZONE 24 px, MAX_PX 90 px linear ramp, auto-centre on release, NEVER fires, NEVER writes pointer.ndc); RIGHT = aim (ndc via aimFromPoint on down + move) + fire while down + FIRE_TAIL 0.22 s on release; 2-finger pause = second finger in the same zone (PAUSE_COOLDOWN 0.45 s + confirm); cross-zone = thrust + fire, no pause; 3rd+ fingers ignored; duplicate same-id pointerdown = no-op; onBlur clears all. New getters: touchDrag (null in deadzone) + rightAimActive.
- src/main.js: createInput now { onPause: togglePause, onPauseConfirm: toast }; resolveAimPoint priority = rightAimActive (raycast ndc) -> touchDrag (aim along the drag, ST-033 carryover) -> pointer.active raycast; + window.__vr.input probe handle.
- UI copy: tutorialHint "LEFT: DRAG TO FLY · RIGHT: AIM + FIRE · 2-FINGER PAUSE"; screens.js + tutorialOverlay.js control rows -> LEFT ZONE / RIGHT ZONE / 2 FINGERS.

Code:
- src/main.js: vendor lowp capability-warning guard. First occurrence of three.js r160 "THREE.WebGLProgram.getParameters: ... not supported, using ..." passes through (observable once); repeats are suppressed (it re-fires per recompiled program, e.g. after a context restore); every occurrence tallied to eventTally.vendorLowpWarn + __vr.vendorLowpWarns(). Root cause (documented): vendor/three.module.js:20618 (r160 WebGLPrograms.getParameters) fires when a program compiles in a GL context whose max fragment precision degraded to "lowp" (degraded GPU window state - occluded/throttled windows where the driver reports zero range for highp/mediump). Benign: three.js falls back to the max supported precision and rendering stays correct; no project material sets .precision (grep-verified) so only an internal (precision: undefined) material can trigger it; NOT reproducible at HEAD in a healthy window (6 natural attempts, 0 hits).

## I287 - ST-271 build minify pass: esbuild per-module, src-only, no bundling (cgs-dev-story, E24 1/4)

Goal: relieve the dist budget crisis discovered while scoping E24 (I286: 2038.0 KB / headroom 10.0 KB vs the ST floor of 8 KB = 2.0 KB usable) before the 7-emblem COLOR_0 bake lands (~+6.5 KB), WITHOUT breaking the no-bundler import-map convention (AGENTS.md: import maps + vendored modules).

What was done:
- npm i -D esbuild (0.28.2; postinstall script policy-blocked but the JS API works - platform binary resolves; node_modules/ gitignored, not committed).
- scripts/build.mjs: + minifyDir(dist/src) BEFORE the vendor copy - walks dist/src/**, each .js through esbuild.transform(read, {loader:'js', format:'esm', minify:true, keepNames:true, legalComments:'none'}) -> write back in place. Per-module only: NO bundling, NO cross-module tree-shaking - every src module keeps its dist path, the import-map convention is preserved; vendor/ + assets/ are never touched.
- Pre-grep (I286): no eval( / new Function / Function( in src/**/*.js, so the minify is syntax-level (local identifiers + whitespace); string literals + property names untouched.

## I311 - ST-290 boss attack telegraph pass (cgs-dev-story, E29 1/3, RENDER-LAYER ONLY 0 KB)

**Summary.** Boss attacks (Monolith ring 2.0s / aimed 2.2s / radial 4.0s; Splicer aimed 2.6s) all fired instantly with no anticipation phase - the sweep-grounded gap (Inner Chaos aipti2jj6ek anticipation/hit/recovery, Universal Player Combat color-coded telegraph markers, Helldivers 2 telegraphing FSHlyBfqc4c). Added a pure render-layer telegraph that reads the public attack timers (`world.boss.ringTimer` / `bossFireTimer` / `bossBurstTimer` - no new state, no sim change) and warns the player before each attack lands.

**Story goal.** Every boss attack gets a visible, readable, fx-gated warning in its final window so "sudden death" becomes "readable threat": (1) RING - expanding floor ring at the boss base growing to the blast radius; (2) AIMED - the boss core seam leans red and brightens toward the player; (3) RADIAL BURST - core pulse + ring pre-flash. All three are data-driven in `CONFIG.boss.telegraph` and pooled/reused (no per-frame allocation).

**Acceptance tests (all met).**
- Ring telegraph: 0.6s window; scale 3.4 + 5.6*teleUrgency(p,1.6) -> measured 5.2473 at p=0.30 and 8.2722 at p=0.05 (near max); opacity 0.35 * min(1, 3p) -> 0.35 peak. Floor ring at teleHeight 0.35.
- Aimed telegraph: 0.5s window; corePulse = p^2 * 0.9 -> coreIntensity 1.2270 (baseline) to 1.5510 at p=0.20 probe point; red-lean 0.6 confirmed by hex shift 9a6bff -> b665e6 (R 154->182 up, B 255->230 down = red lean).
- Burst telegraph: 0.8s window; coreBoost 1.4 -> coreIntensity 2.1020 at p=0.30; ring pre-flash scale 10 / opacity 0.1375.
- Gating: fx-off tier -> zero telegraph leak (F5: ringT 0.233 in window, all hidden). fx-low -> telegraph RETAINED (F6a direct + F6b real-loop: informational, not decorative - stinger precedent keeps telegraph, gates wobble). No boss -> all hidden.
- No sim impact: by layer only - no sim/scoring/replay data touched; demo pin structurally safe and re-verified exactly.

**Changed files.**
- `src/core/bossTelegraph.js` (NEW, ~40 LOC) - pure math: teleProgress / teleUrgency helpers (DOM-free, unit-testable).
- `src/core/config.js` - `CONFIG.boss.telegraph` block: ring{window 0.6, maxRadius 9.0, opacity 0.35}, aimed{window 0.5, coreBoost 0.9, redLean 0.6}, burst{window 0.8, coreBoost 1.4, ringRadius 10.0, opacity 0.22}. Threat red = `CONFIG.fx.enemyBullet.emissive` (0xff4a2a).
- `src/render/bossMesh.js` - `sync(boss, t, ringP, aimP, burstP)` telegraph pass: ring mesh (pooled torus geometry), core seam red-lean + intensity, burst pre-flash; `telestate()` readback for verification.
- `src/main.js` - `teleOn` fx-gate (tier-aware: off -> 0, low/med/high -> live timers); passes timer-derived progress into bossMesh.sync each frame.
- `tests/bossTelegraph.test.js` (NEW) - 6 cases: windows, urgency curve monotonicity, boundary clamps, no-leak at window edges.

## I312 - ST-291 engine presentation audit + warm->cool trail ramp (cgs-dev-story, E29 2/3, RENDER-LAYER 0 KB)

**Summary.** The queued ship engine/thrust trail already exists (I213 trail 14 puffs/s + ST-256 layered flame + ST-237 nozzle), so ST-291 was a probe-first audit (designated CUTTABLE). AUDIT: 3 of 4 sweep criteria PASS, 1 PARTIAL - the "bright->dim tail / palette.engine warm->cool" was implemented as a per-particle RANDOM palette pick (particles.js burst() `tmp.set(pal[(Math.random()*pal.length)|0])`), not a warm-core->cool-tail age gradient, so the trail read as a warm/cool sparkle mix rather than a smooth gradient.

**Story goal.** Make the engine trail read as a hot (warm) core fading to a cool tail along the puff lifetime - data-driven, render-layer only, 0 KB, no sim/scoring/replay change.

**Acceptance tests (all met).**
- Thrust-reactive rate: minThrust 0.12 gate + rate 14 puffs/s (deterministic accumulator) - PASS (no change).
- World-space lag: puffs spawn at ship.pos - forward*offset(1.15) in WORLD coords, ship moves on, drag exp(-3dt) - PASS (no change).
- ST-256 core/plume layering: hot white core (0xffffff op0.95 r0.10 len0.70) inside warm orange plume (0xff9a3d op0.65 r0.28 len1.25) + additive glow sprite (0xffb347 op0.40 size1.1) at nozzle root, all data-driven via CONFIG.ship.flame - PASS (no change).
- bright->dim tail: PARTIAL -> FIXED. particles.burst/sync now honor `o.ramp`: per-particle color lerps pal[0] (warm 0xffa860) -> pal[last] (cool 0x9fd8ff) by normalized age (shared per-particle brightness jitter), then the existing bright->dim fade (color * (1-age/life)). Gated by new CONFIG.fx.engineTrail.ramp (true).

**Changed files.**
- `src/render/particles.js` - added `base2` (Float32Array POOL*3) + `rampFlag` (Uint8Array POOL); burst() sets base=pal[0]/base2=pal[last] when o.ramp (else the ST-086 random pick, flag 0); sync() lerps base->base2 by age/life when rampFlag (else base*f). No per-frame allocs; non-ramp path behavior unchanged.
- `src/core/config.js` - `CONFIG.fx.engineTrail.ramp: true` (data-driven toggle, comment cites ST-291).
- `src/main.js` - engine-trail burst passes `ramp: CONFIG.fx.engineTrail.ramp`.
- BOM hygiene: an edit-tool artifact dropped one U+FEFF BOM from the leading line of config.js (4->3) and main.js (3->2) during the I312 edits; restored to the committed prefix so the committed diff carries only the intended changes.

**Verification evidence.**

## I315 - ST-293 arena floor readability micro-pass (cgs-dev-story, E30 1/3)
- Summary: Audit-first. Pre-registered decision rule: measure the on-screen floor band luma (PLAYING + MENU fx-off) and take the TUNE branch only if the hub->mid-arena drop exceeded 15% of the hub->rim total (i.e. no distinct rest band read). MEASURED baseline: the single-pow radial grid (falloffPow 1.6) produced a SMOOTH monotone fade in PLAYING - lineP90 across 10 radial bands b1..b9 = 50.7/46.3/41.9/38.7/34.8/31.6/28.5/22.9/18.8 (no plateau; hub->mid drop 31.5% of the hub->rim total) -> rule FAILED -> TUNE branch. Implementation = a pure 2-segment curve restFalloff(t,restT,restHold,restPowA,restPowB) in floorGrid.js + restGridColorAt, driven by 4 new CONFIG.arena.grid tunables (restT 0.5 / restHold 0.76 / restPowA 0.05 / restPowB 2.0); legacy falloff/gridColorAt retained (still unit-tested). arenaFloor.js ring-stops + spoke-stops now call restGridColorAt. ## I320 - ST-297 adaptive-toast anchor fix (cgs-dev-story, E31 2/3, BY LAYER, +11 B)

**Goal.** Fix R3 finding #1 from the I319 ST-296 battery: #adaptive-toast overlapped #tutorial-hint (1380 px^2 at 720p). Single-line render/DOM change; no sim/scoring/replay touch (BY LAYER - the demo pin is structurally safe).

**Fix.** src/main.js:283 - toastEl cssText `bottom:64px` -> `bottom:calc(9% + 40px)`. The hint bar (#tutorial-hint) is pinned at bottom:9% (~20px tall, 15px font); anchoring the toast to the same 9% reference keeps the clearance constant at every viewport height (40px anchor - 20px hint = 20px gap at 720p, 800px, 480p alike). Toast stays centered (left:50%, translateX(-50%)), z60, same styling; all 11 toast() call sites share the element, so every callout (FX / MUSIC / RECORDING / PAUSED / INBOUND / WEAPON LEVEL / RUN SAVED) moves with it.

## I321 - ST-299 wave banner hidden on GAME_OVER (cgs-dev-story, E31 3/3, BY LAYER, +121 B)

**Goal.** Fix R3 finding #2 from the I319 ST-296 battery: the wave banner ("WAVE n" / "CLEARED" / boss bar) remained visible on the GAME OVER screen, overlapping the GAME OVER title (6804 px^2 at 720p). Render/DOM-only change; no sim/scoring/replay touch (BY LAYER - the demo pin is structurally safe).

**Fix.** src/render/waveBanner.js + src/main.js:897. sync() now takes the game state as a 4th argument and force-hides the banner (clears anim + text, opacity 0) via a new resetHidden() helper when state === STATE.GAME_OVER; the same helper is reused on the natural anim-expiry path (behavior there unchanged). main.js passes world.game.state. Because sync() runs on every syncVisuals (live frame AND probe advance()), the banner is guaranteed hidden by the death-frame render - even when the banner anim is mid-envelope at the instant of death. That mid-envelope hold is exactly the I319 failure state: with rAF frozen, each advance() advances the banner t by only one STEP, so an armed banner stayed at opacity 1 indefinitely.

(2) Flow = peaks and troughs with respite; perceived stress = threat count x proximity, per player, director targets low-stress players; post-panic the director refrains from spawning AND swaps item spawns based on player performance (WbHMxo11HcU [2:58][5:28][6:03][8:39]). - Wiring delivered (0 KB to main.js - director is core, imported by game.js which is already in dist):
  - waves.js: onDecide(wave) hook + activeAdj/activeMod/openGate public fields; new _modFor(wave) maps the director modifier bias (gentle avoids fast+inward -> none; hard -> prefer[wave%len]; breather -> none; no adj -> base seeded mod); toSpawn = round(contentFor(wave) * activeAdj.d).
  - game.js: World now constructs its own SkillModel + Director; waves.onDecide = dir.decideForWave (replayMode from the replay state); per-step skill.sample(dt, load) + director.sample(dt, load); enemyBullets.speedMul = activeAdj.b; a shipDamage() helper wraps the 7 livesMgr.damage() call sites and also fires skill.onEvent(hit, {lives}) + director.onEvent(hit, {lives}); the 4 kill sites fire skill.onEvent(kill, {weight}); shots fire shot; nearmiss fires graze; 2x maybeDrop(..., dropMul()) use activeAdj.drop; reset() resets skill + director + speedMul.
  - powerups.js: maybeDrop(pos, dropMul). enemyBullets.js: speedMul field (multiplies bolt speed when set by the director).
- Seam-test rewrite (tests/directorWiring.test.js, 5 tests):
  - smoke: a passive pilot (thrust {x:0,y:1}) never cleared the field, so waves only stall-advanced (45 s each) and wave 3 (director firstWave) was never reached in 3600 ticks -> replaced with a seek-and-shoot-nearest-rock pilot and bumped ticks 3600 -> 4500 (wave 3 first starts ~tick 3834).
  - 4 seam tests: the 2.2 s initial intermission is 132 ticks at DT=1/60, so a 10-step loop cannot even start wave 1 -> all 4 now use a primeStart(dir, target, onDecide) direct-set helper (dir.wave=target-1; toSpawn=0; state=intermission; intermission=0; return step(DT)) that isolates the exact wave-start transition.
  - density test: toSpawn is clobbered by the spawn loop in the same step a wave starts -> fill the field ABOVE the wave-3 concurrent limit (12) AFTER clearing and BEFORE the step, so the spawn loop is suppressed and toSpawn stays at round(contentFor(3)=7 * 0.5) = 4.
  - gentle test: the old pin (seed 3042 base mod = fast) was WRONG (it is big) -> re-pinned to seed 3040 (verified base mod fast for wave 3; gentle avoids fast -> none).
  - Verified pins: hard alternation wave3 -> inward (prefer[3%2]) / wave4 -> fast (prefer[4%2]); prefer = [fast, inward]; breather (everyWave=2) wave 3 stays none even under hard.

Density/mod trajectory waves 3->8: 0.891/none -> 0.994/none -> 1.097/hard -> LULL 0.6/gentle (a hit, d=0.6) -> 0.753/gentle -> 0.856/none. It escalates for skilled play (density 0.89 -> 1.10, mod -> hard), snaps to a lull at wave 6, then recovers (+0.15 pressure/wave); final pressure 0.400, final skillP 1.000.

## I351 - ST-321 E38 floating-stick visual (cgs-dev-story; render/DOM + 1 pure core extension)

Goal: ship ST-321 - the on-screen floating thrust-stick visual so the player can see the LEFT-zone stick's origin and how much thrust is applied (G1: it was purely virtual - no ring, no knob anywhere).

Scope: render/DOM layer + exactly one PURE src/core extension (knobOffset) + its unit tests. BY LAYER - zero src/core sim/scoring/replay logic touched, zero three.js in core, the demo pin is structurally untouched (causally re-verified).

What shipped:
- src/core/touchZones.js: new PURE knobOffset(dx, dy, deadzone, maxPx) -> {x, y, mag, active}. Mirrors the finger drag, clamps to the full-thrust radius (maxPx) keeping the unit direction, mag = |d|/maxPx (0..1), active = |d| > deadzone. No DOM, no three (unit-testable).
- src/render/input.js: export DEADZONE 24 / MAX_PX 90 (now shared with the visual); new read-only get leftStick() returning the reused leftStickOut {active, sx, sy, dx, dy} (no per-frame alloc) derived from the existing leftTouch.
- src/render/touchStick.js (NEW, 3648 B): createTouchStick() builds #vr-touch-stick (position:fixed, z-index 29, pointer-events none) + a 180 px ring (border rgba(207,228,255,0.35)) + a 48 px knob (bg rgba(207,228,255,0.55)). sync(input, dt, visible) reads input.leftStick each frame, positions the root at the origin via translate3d and the knob via knobOffset; knob opacity 1 when active / 0.45 faint inside the dead-zone; fade-in 0.12 s / fade-out 0.20 s; display none at fade 0; returns the reused out readout. dispose() removes the node. Geometry is 1:1 with viewport px (NOT --vr-fs scaled) so the knob always sits exactly under the finger.
- src/main.js: createTouchStick() only when coarse (zero DOM on mouse/keyboard); touchStick.sync(input, dt, st === STATE.PLAYING) in syncVisuals - fades out on non-PLAYING, and input.js clears leftTouch on pointercancel/blur so the stick hides for free.

## I366 - ST-334 starfield-knot correlation: correlate the twinkling Points starfield with the v6 knots (cgs-dev-story; probe 22/22, battery 13/13 MATCH PASS)

Goal: denser / slightly brighter twinkling stars over the dominant core knot (u=0.65, lat 4 deg) + a soft secondary knot (u=0.18, lat 4 deg), sparser elsewhere - star count, per-star RNG call budget (fixed 7) and the isolated starfield RNG stream preserved so the p1 demo pin stays EXACT.

Design (final): 3-way mix sampler, count-preserving, fixed 7 RNG calls/star:
- Per star: t = rng.next(); t < 0.25 -> core knot; t < 0.30 -> secondary; else uniform (byte-identical to the pre-I366 stream: u = rng.next()*2-1, theta = rng.next()*2*PI).
- Knot draw (Box-Muller, 2 calls): Gaussian in u_tex (sigma = sizeUDeg/360) + latitude (sigma = sizeLatDeg*D2R); u_tex wrapped with floor; azimuth = (ut - 0.5) * 2*PI (equirect convention: az = (u_tex - 0.5) * 360 deg, +x toward +z); pre-flatten u back-solved from latitude: v = sin^2(latC), u = sign(latC) * sqrt(v / (0.49 + 0.51*v)) (derived from the rendered y*0.7 flatten: sin(lat) = 0.7u/sqrt(1-0.51u^2)).
- Brightness boost: core 1.15x, secondary 1.12x (aScale = rng.range(0.7, 1.4) * bright).
- Render (src/render/starfield.js): shaders, geometry layout, materials, group.update, createStarfield API behavior-identical; only the direction draw inside makeShell changed. Two bugs found + fixed pre-probe: wrap must be floor (round is only right for differences), and theta = (ut - 0.5) * 2*PI (not ut * 2*PI - u_tex 0.5 is +z... the equirect 0.5 center maps to az 0 = +x).

DEVIATION from the handoff plan (documented): the previous plan was rejection sampling (per-star accept = base + boost*w, count-preserving bias of uniform draws toward the knot). Pre-sim (.evidence/I366/presim.mjs) proved it invisible: the 12x8 deg core knot covers ~0.46% of the sphere; with 800 stars a count-preserving rejection bias (boost <= 1-base) adds only ~2 stars into the knot region - pre-sim core/antipode ratio 1.0, bright stars 0 (design expected 1.3-1.8) - so the acceptance "correlation visible in screenshots" would have failed. The mix sampler allocates 25%/5% of stars directly to the clumps (same count, same 7-call budget) -> measured core 11/5 + 128/61.
